No. The owner did not authorize cutting tests to speed things up. He objected only to useless tests and to repeated CI runs.

After I cancelled tests, he said (user): "Btw I never said u shoukd cancel tests etc...", "I'm just against useless tests", and "repeating the same ci cd process multiple times for no reason". I admitted I had misread him and restored the cut tests.

Earlier he wrote, via a handoff: "I will not accept such long and wasteful ci cd processes any longer!"

The rules that followed are:
- Run each check once per tree.
- Remove useless tests, but leave webkit-caw and across-update alone.
- Keep the 25 ms target; don't relax thresholds.

He also said (user): "Bro you don't have to edit the owner rules".
